basics.name: Jonas Kemnitzer
basics.label: Research Associate & PhD-track Researcher
basics.summary: PhD-track researcher at IISYS Hof University focusing on LLM security, mechanistic interpretability, and multimodal AI systems. Experienced in bridging academic research with industry deployment for SMEs.

work.name: IISYS at Hof University of Applied Sciences
work.summary: Researched and developed multimodal AI systems within the Intelligent and Learning Systems group, covering the full stack from multi-GPU model training and fine-tuning to production inference deployment.
highlights: Bridged academic research and industry application by transferring AI solutions into active production environments for small and medium-sized German businesses.

Conducted research in mechanistic interpretability, applying circuit analysis techniques to locate and characterise attention heads causally responsible for prompt injection in instruction-tuned LLMs.

work.name: IBM Germany
work.summary: Developed anomaly detection pipelines on large-scale infrastructure datasets for road and bridge safety analysis using Python and Apache Spark on IBM Cloud.
highlights: Designed and deployed a customer-facing conversational AI system on a Pepper robot, integrating IBM Watson Assistant with live APIs and custom dialogue flows for lobby guest interaction.
Collaborated with solution architects to prototype and refine customer-oriented AI demos across multiple client engagements.

volunteer.organization: Students Union, Hof University of Applied Sciences
volunteer.summary: Represented faculty of computer science students, organised events, and acted as a freshman mentor during newcomer days.

publications.name: Beyond shared embedding spaces: Towards LLM architectures with explicit authority control for prompt security
publications.summary: Proposes LLM architectures with explicit authority control mechanisms to defend against prompt injection attacks in instruction-tuned models. To appear at the 2026 International Conference on Advances in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AAIML), Tokyo, Japan.

publications.name: Enhancing Fitness Visualization: Application and Efficacy of Realistic Inpainting Techniques using Diffusion Models
publications.summary: Presents a stable-diffusion based zero-shot approach to realistically transform the image of a human body into a more fit version of that depicted person, combining a modified stable diffusion model with inpainting techniques and incorporated constraints.

projects.name: Explainable AI (LIME)
projects.summary: Implemented and analysed the Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) algorithm in Python, evaluating input parameter sensitivity on the YouTube Comments Spam Dataset to reduce data complexity through systematic parameter optimisation.

projects.name: Sentiment Analysis using NLP
projects.summary: Built a proof-of-concept sentiment analysis pipeline for an online retail use case using Python, TensorFlow, and Keras, benchmarking multiple frameworks for performance trade-offs and refactoring the codebase to reduce overall runtime overhead.
